title: Diagnostics
description: Persisted model quality evidence. Computed once at fit time and read thereafter; every metric is reported for train AND holdout side by side (02 FR-170, FR-171, FR-172, FR-174, FR-182, FR-183, FR-184, FR-186, FR-187).
$comment: Amended 2026-08-22 (WK-661, the contract-reconciliation slice). The `gbm` block differed from `GbmDiagnostics` in name, shape or cardinality on almost every field, and none of it was visible: the type comparison skips a path that exists on only one side, which is what a rename or a re-shape produces. Resolutions, each the code's (CLAUDE.md §0): `backtest` is deleted — it was declared from Phase 0, typed None, and nothing could ever have populated it, because FR-187's backtest runs against a LATER Dataset Version than the one this artifact is written for; it is its own artifact now (§4.12). `double_lift` is deleted from the partition for the same reason at a different scale — it is pairwise, the comparison model is unknown at fit time, and it lives on the comparison artifact. `importance` becomes `importances` keyed by `feature`, and `permutation_holdout` becomes the six-field `permutation_importances`, which carries the provenance a single number cannot. `partial_dependence_blob` becomes structured per-factor points, `monotonicity_verified` becomes a tuple of per-factor checks, and `tree_summary` becomes `tree_count`/`max_depth`/`mean_depth` — a forest of stumps with one deep tree and a forest of uniformly middling trees have the same mean. `best_iteration` is deleted: it lives on the fit result because `predict_gbm` needs it to score and diagnostics are not loaded at scoring time. `quantile_crossing` is added, which FR-199 requires be reported in the diagnostics and this contract had no property for at all. The `cross_validation` block is rebuilt around what FR-112/182 actually persist.

job_id.description: The job that computed these diagnostics, where one did.

universal.description: A diagnostic reported without its holdout counterpart is a defect (FR-183). Both partitions must share a weighting scheme: comparing an exposure-weighted train A/E to an unweighted holdout A/E is comparing two quantities and reading the difference as deterioration (FR-184).

glm.description: FR-172. Null for a non-GLM fit.

aic.description: Null where the family has no closed-form likelihood this platform evaluates (Tweedie needs a series expansion). A deviance-based stand-in would differ from another tool's AIC by an additive constant, which reads as a disagreement between two correct numbers.

gbm.description: FR-174's GBM-specific evidence. Null for a GLM, which is the honest reading of 'GBM-specific'.

eval_curve.description: Train and holdout on one row rather than two series: a metric still improving on train while flat on holdout is the shape early stopping exists to catch, and two separately-stored series can be joined wrongly.

permutation_importances.description: Its own measurement, not a column on the importance row: a permutation score is only readable beside the baseline it degraded from, the repeat count and the seed.

partial_dependence.description: Per declared factor, and structured — this was an opaque blob string until 2026-08-22, which no reader could plot without unpacking it first.

monotonicity.description: One check per constrained factor, carrying the worst violation. A single boolean cannot say which factor failed, and `TransparencyArtifact.monotonicity_verified` is where the rolled-up answer belongs.

mean_depth.description: Beside `max_depth`, not instead of it: a forest of stumps with one deep tree and a forest of uniformly middling trees have the same mean.

quantile_crossing.description: FR-199. Set on the SECOND bound of a paired-quantile interval and null on every other model, including the first bound, which had nothing to cross when it was fitted.

cross_validation.description: The penalty path and the selected alpha's fold dispersion (FR-112, FR-182). Populated iff the fit's `select_by == 'cv'`; null for every fixed-alpha GLM and every GBM — the honest reading of 'this fit was not cross-validated' rather than an empty path standing in for one.

method.description: UNRECONCILED (WK-661, 2026-08-22): this contract declared `fold_construction` with a closed set — random | temporal | grouped_by_key — matching FR-182, `01` FR-73 and `GlmCvSpec.method`'s own enum, while `CrossValidationDiagnostics.method` is an unconstrained `str`. Renamed to the built field and widened here so the contract does not promise a constraint nothing enforces; whether the type should close instead is a CLAUDE.md §0 question.

seed.description: The seed `assign_folds` was called with, copied here so the fold assignment is reproducible from this artifact alone, with no join back to the spec.

folds.description: The fold COUNT. This contract declared an array of unnamed objects under the same name until 2026-08-22; the per-fold records are `fold_metrics`.

metric.description: Always `deviance` today — the fitted family's own — recorded rather than assumed.

complexity.description: Recorded on every fit, beside whatever thresholds were in force (FR-185). The thresholds are stored with the measurements because they are workspace settings that change: a fit judged against no limit and one judged against a limit of 40 are different events.

max_factor_count.description: The workspace limit in force, or null where none is set — FR-185's default. Distinct from 0, which would be a limit nothing could satisfy.

invariants: universal.train.weighting == universal.holdout.weighting — side-by-side metrics must share a weighting scheme (FR-184)
every eval_curve point reports at least one of train and holdout
cross_validation.selected_alpha is one of cross_validation.path[].alpha — the selection must be a point the path actually scored
cross_validation.fold_metrics covers folds 0..folds-1 exactly once: a fold's dispersion cannot include a fold that was never scored, nor double-count one

weighting.description: Explicit; an unweighted metric on an exposure-weighted problem is labelled as such (FR-184).

MonotonicityCheck.description: That the fitted response actually respects a declared constraint, not merely that it was passed to the backend.

QuantileCrossing.description: Whether this bound contradicts its counterpart over the fit population (FR-199). Crossing means the pair does not describe one distribution; it is reported, never silently reordered.
